chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh ibn Nusayr, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid and others, they said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
May Allah have mercy on Zurara ibn A'yan; if it were not for Zurara and his peers, the narrations of my father (peace be upon him) would have perished.

key_terms.أَحَادِيثُ: Plural of hadith, referring to the narrations and sayings of the Prophet or Imams.
key_terms.ابْنُ أَعْيَنَ: Ibn A'yan, the patronymic of Zurara.
key_terms.زُرَارَةُ: Zurara, a prominent companion of the Imams known for his extensive narrations.
key_terms.نُظَرَاؤُهُ: His peers or contemporaries, referring to other key narrators of the same era.

ai.seo_question: Why is Zurara ibn A'yan considered essential for the preservation of Imam Muhammad al-Baqir's narrations?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kashi's *Rijal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates Zurara ibn A'yan and his peers as the primary custodians of the Imams' teachings, asserting that their scholarly rigor prevented the loss of prophetic traditions. This statement underscores the Shia concept of *Tawatur* (mass transmission) through specific, reliable scholars, validating the authority of the *Usul* (foundational hadiths) compiled by these key narrators.

en.ammaar-muslim: 4. [4/160] Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh b. Nusayr from Ya`qub b. Yazid and Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi al-Khattab from Muhammad b. Abi Umayr from Ibrahim b. Abd al-Hamid and others apart from him – they all said: Abu Abdillah عليه السلام said:
may Allah have mercy on Zurara b. A`yan, if it was not for Zurara and his peers the narrations of my father عليه السلام would have perished.
